expectations.text: The verdict is approve or approve with comments, not changes requested
No comment is labelled or phrased as blocking
expectations.evidence: No blocking comments; one praise, one question, two suggestions, one nit.

expectations.text: The review does not claim the f-string ORDER BY is a SQL injection vulnerability (it may mention that it is safe because of the whitelist)
expectations.evidence: Says the dynamic ORDER BY is fine because of the whitelist.

expectations.text: The review does not flag the INVOICE_EXPORT_TOKEN environment variable read as a hardcoded secret
expectations.evidence: Does not call the env var read a hardcoded secret; asks where the route checks it.

expectations.text: The review gives specific credit for something the author did well, such as the sort whitelist or the injection test
expectations.evidence: Praise on the whitelist and the injection test.

expectations.text: The review contains no more than three nit or suggestion comments in total

suggestions.assertion: The verdict is approve or approve with comments, not changes requested
suggestions.reason: Both runs found an unplanted but real issue: LIMIT/OFFSET over a non-unique ORDER BY can repeat or drop rows. Requiring approve penalises a correct catch. Reword to 'does not raise a false security alarm'.

eval_feedback.overall: The discriminating part of this case is severity calibration, which the assertions do not capture.
